commit.message:
Claude/actenon kernel mcp setup qolk0h (#2)

* fix: fail closed on shell expansions blastradius does not model

resolve_target only expands plain $VAR and ${VAR}. Any other expansion
left in the target after that pass — ${VAR:-/}, ${VAR:=/}, ${VAR:+x},
${#VAR}, ${VAR%pattern}, $1, $$, $@ — was passed through as a literal
filename and then judged in-scope, so it was ALLOWED. In a real shell
those forms produce a concrete path we never computed:

  rm -rf ${UNSET:-/}   # deletes / in bash; blastradius allowed it

This violates principle 2 (fail closed). Now, if a `$` survives variable
expansion, the target cannot be resolved with certainty and is refused
with a new unoverridable rule `unresolvable-expansion`. Plain $VAR /
${VAR} continue to expand normally, so in-scope deletions are unaffected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* fix: catch destructive commands behind wrappers and git global options

identify_destructive only inspected tokens[0], so any command runner in
front of rm hid it entirely. Every one of these was ALLOWED to hit a
floor path on main:

  sudo rm -rf /etc      env rm -rf /etc      xargs rm -rf /etc
  nice / nohup / setsid / exec / command / doas / busybox / ionice /
  stdbuf rm ...         timeout 5 rm -rf /etc     sudo rm -rf $HOME

Added _unwrap_wrappers(): it strips leading command-runner wrappers
(and their options/arguments, env NAME=VAL assignments, and the
timeout DURATION positional), recursing through nested wrappers, before
identification. It returns the tokens unchanged when the inner command
cannot be located, so unwrapping can only ever ADD a block, never remove
one. Applied to both identify_destructive and identify_risks.

Also fixed three narrower escapes:

- git global options before the subcommand (git -C / clean -fdx,
  git --git-dir=x --work-tree=/ reset --hard) hid the destructive
  subcommand from the args[0] == "clean"/"reset" check. Added
  _git_split() to parse global options and honour -C / --work-tree /
  --git-dir as the operative target directory.
- find -execdir rm was not detected (only -exec was).
- truncate with a glued size flag (truncate -s0 FILE) was not detected
  because the guard tested exact membership of "-s" in the flag list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* test: adversarial bypass regression suite (wrappers, git, expansions)

One test per confirmed bypass, each of which was ALLOWED on the parent
commit and is now a BLOCK: wrapper prefixes (F1), git global-option
escapes (F2), unmodelled shell expansions (F3), find -execdir (F4), and
truncate with a glued size flag (F5). Includes must-allow guards proving
the fixes do not over-block in-scope wrapped deletions or plain $VAR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* docs: correct README test count, rule table, and coverage notes

- The "128 tests" figure was stale (the suite is 198). Updated.
- Added the unresolvable-expansion rule to the rule reference table.
- Documented in the Identify/Resolve steps that command-runner wrappers
  are unwrapped, git global options are honoured, and expansions beyond
  $VAR/${VAR} are refused fail-closed — matching actual behaviour.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* ci: add test workflow running the suite on Python 3.10-3.12

The repo had only publish.yml (tags). Added ci.yml running the full test
suite on push/PR across the supported Python versions, matching the
sibling Actenon repos' Python CI style.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* fix(eval-agent): make the isolation proof pass when run as root

The proof overlaid a tmpfs on /home to hide the host home canary, but a
root invocation has ~ = /root, which is not under /home, so TEST2
("host home canary is readable") failed. Overlay a tmpfs on the invoking
user's actual home directory as well, so the proof holds for any user.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

---------
